data.change_summary: Finalized the habitat-registry amendments by making substrate habitats depth-aware, deriving plant crowding during registry refreshes, using the actual water column above the substrate for substrate-surface light attenuation, documenting the intentional post-clogging daily refresh, and gating post-action habitat refreshes to habitat-affecting actions only. Added regressions covering zero-depth substrate handling, depth/kind-sensitive deep-substrate area, biomass-driven light shading, substrate-surface light sensitivity to substrate depth, trim-driven crowding/light refresh, and light-action refresh behavior.
outstanding_risks: Validation was targeted, not full-workspace; I ran the habitat, save/load, plant-algae, and scenario materialization/override suites, but not the entire repository test matrix.

Substrate deep-area scaling now relies on kind-level colonizable-area factors encoded on `SubstrateKind`; those values should stay aligned with the substrate preset pack until a first-class serialized per-layer factor exists.

steps.description: Inspected the current habitat registry, engine refresh paths, substrate/model inputs, and scenario materialization to map each pending amendment to concrete code paths.

Updated habitat/state/action logic so registry rebuilds recompute crowding and substrate-derived areas, substrate-surface light uses water above the bed, daily dual-refresh intent is documented, and post-action refreshes only run for habitat-relevant actions.

Expanded habitat regression coverage for zero-depth substrate, depth- and kind-sensitive substrate deep area, biomass-driven shading, substrate-depth light response, trim-driven crowding refresh, and light-action refresh behavior.
Validated the amended behavior across targeted core and scenario suites, including save/load and algae integration paths affected by the habitat-model changes.

validation_evidence: `cargo test -p tank_scenarios --test materialization --test startup_overrides` passed (9 materialization tests, 4 startup-override tests).
